newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Firms vie for $600 mln airport contracts in UAE.
newsitem.headline: Firms vie for $600 mln airport contracts in UAE.

text.p: International firms are vying for consultancy contracts for a $600 million expansion at Abu Dhabi and al-Ain airports in the United Arab Emirates, Abdullah Bilhaif al-Nuaimi, Abu Dhabi Department of Civil Aviation's director of engineering and maintenance said on Wednesday.
Abu Dhabi airport, which serves 43 airlines, is hoping the expansion will help increase its yearly passenger flow to seven million by the year 2000 from a current 3.2 million.
Passenger traffic rose 13 percent in the past year, al-Nuaimi said.
"We want to become a major regional hub," he said. "We also want to be seen as a link between East and West, an international hub," he said.
Abu Dhabi will face stiff competition from the neighbouring emirate of Dubai, a regional trade and re-export hub with the Gulf's busiest airport.

But Nuaimi said Abu Dhabi has embarked on a more agressive marketing drive and is vying to host aviation conferences to boost its image. "We are approaching more airlines to inform them of what we have to offer."
